value.behaviour: Export styled text runs as `<tspan>` child nodes and inline background highlights as `<rect>` nodes in `renderElementToSvg` when `element.textStyleRanges` is non-empty.
rules: 1. Import `getFontString` from `@excalidraw/common` and import `getLineWidth` and `getTextElementLineRuns` alongside `getLineHeightInPx` from `@excalidraw/element`.

2. In `renderElementToSvg` for `isTextElement(element)`, when `!element.textStyleRanges?.length`, execute the existing loop emitting `<text>` nodes with `text.textContent = lines[i]` unchanged (NFR-3).
3. When `element.textStyleRanges?.length` is non-zero, compute `font = getFontString(element)` and `lineRuns = getTextElementLineRuns(element, renderConfig.renderEnvironment)`.

4. For each visual line `i`, compute `lineText = lines[i] ?? ""`, `runs = lineRuns[i] ?? [{ text: lineText, start: 0, end: lineText.length }]`, `lineWidth = getLineWidth(lineText, font, renderConfig.renderEnvironment)`, and `lineStartX = element.textAlign === "center" ? (element.width - lineWidth) / 2 : element.textAlign === "right" ? element.width - lineWidth : 0`.

5. Before appending the line's `<text>` node to `node`, for each run in `runs` with a non-empty, non-`"transparent"` `backgroundColor` and `run.text.length > 0`, measure `prefixWidth = getLineWidth(prefixText, font, renderConfig.renderEnvironment)` and `runWidth = getLineWidth(run.text, font, renderConfig.renderEnvironment)`, compute `runX = direction === "rtl" ? lineStartX + (lineWidth - prefixWidth - runWidth) : lineStartX + prefixWidth`, create an SVG `<rect>` node (`svgRoot.ownerDocument.createElementNS(SVG_NS, "rect")`) with attributes `x="${runX}"`, `y="${i * lineHeightPx}"`, `width="${runWidth}"`, `height="${lineHeightPx}"`, and `fill="${applyDarkModeFilter(run.backgroundColor, renderConfig.theme === THEME.DARK)}"`, and append it to `node`.

6. For the line's `<text>` node, if `runs.length > 1 || runs.some((r) => !!r.strokeColor)`, append a `<tspan>` child (`svgRoot.ownerDocument.createElementNS(SVG_NS, "tspan")`) for each run with `tspan.textContent = run.text` and (when `run.strokeColor` is defined) `tspan.setAttribute("fill", applyDarkModeFilter(run.strokeColor, renderConfig.theme === THEME.DARK))`; otherwise set `text.textContent = lineText`.

value.behaviour: Track active character selection `[selectionStart, selectionEnd)` in the WYSIWYG textarea, distinguish user/programmatic range selections from the initial mount `editable.select()`, preserve selection across properties panel interactions, and export `getActiveTextWysiwygSelection`.
rules: 1. Maintain module-level state `activeWysiwygSelectionState: { elementId: string; editable: HTMLTextAreaElement; isInitialAutoSelect: boolean; lastSelection: { start: number; end: number } | null } | null = null` and export `getActiveTextWysiwygSelection(element?: Pick<ExcalidrawTextElement, "id" | "originalText"> | null): { start: number; end: number } | null`.

2. In `getActiveTextWysiwygSelection(element)`: return `null` if `!activeWysiwygSelectionState` or `(element && activeWysiwygSelectionState.elementId !== element.id)`; read `start = editable.selectionStart ?? 0` and `end = editable.selectionEnd ?? 0` clamped to `textLength = element?.originalText.length ?? editable.value.length`; if `start !== 0 || end !== editable.value.length`, set `activeWysiwygSelectionState.isInitialAutoSelect = false`; if `!activeWysiwygSelectionState.isInitialAutoSelect && 0 <= start && start < end && end <= textLength`, update `lastSelection = { start, end }` and return `{ start, end }`; otherwise if `!activeWysiwygSelectionState.isInitialAutoSelect && activeWysiwygSelectionState.lastSelection` and `0 <= lastSelection.start < Math.min(lastSelection.end, textLength)`, return `{ start: lastSelection.start, end: Math.min(lastSelection.end, textLength) }`; else return `null`.

3. On editor init in `textWysiwyg`, initialise `activeWysiwygSelectionState` for `element.id` and `editable`: if `initialSelection && initialSelection.start < initialSelection.end`, set `isInitialAutoSelect = false` and `lastSelection = { start: initialSelection.start, end: initialSelection.end }` and apply `editable.setSelectionRange(initialSelection.start, initialSelection.end)`; when `if (autoSelect && !pendingInitialSelection) { editable.select(); }` runs on mount, set `isInitialAutoSelect = true` and `lastSelection = null`.

4. Wrap `editable.setSelectionRange` and define custom `selectionStart`/`selectionEnd` property descriptors on `editable` (delegating to `HTMLTextAreaElement.prototype`) so any post-mount call to `setSelectionRange` or assignment to `selectionStart`/`selectionEnd` (outside internal init/input normalization) clears `isInitialAutoSelect = false` and updates `lastSelection`, and attach `select`, `keyup`, and `pointerup` listeners on `editable` to sync `lastSelection` and clear `isInitialAutoSelect` (calling `app.setState({})` on `select` or `setSelectionRange` when `app.state.editingTextElement` is active so the properties panel reflects the selection).

5. In `onPointerDown`, before `temporarilyDisableSubmit()` when interacting with `.shape-actions-menu`, `.compact-shape-actions-island`, `.properties-trigger`, or `.properties-content`, snapshot the current active selection into `lastSelection` so blurring the textarea does not lose it; in `unbindUpdate`, when refocusing `editable` while `lastSelection` is active and `!isInitialAutoSelect`, restore `editable.setSelectionRange(lastSelection.start, lastSelection.end)` without triggering `isInitialAutoSelect`; in `cleanup()`, clear `activeWysiwygSelectionState` if it belongs to `editable`.

rules: 1. Import `normalizeTextStyleRanges` and `shiftTextStyleRangesOnEdit` from `@excalidraw/element` and `Mutable` from `@excalidraw/common/utility-types`.

2. In `handleTextWysiwyg`'s `updateElement`, when updating `_element.id === latestTextElement.id && isTextElement(_element)`, compute `nextTextStyleRanges = _element.originalText === nextOriginalText ? normalizeTextStyleRanges(_element.textStyleRanges, nextOriginalText.length, _element.strokeColor) : shiftTextStyleRangesOnEdit(_element.textStyleRanges, _element.originalText, nextOriginalText)` and pass `textStyleRanges: nextTextStyleRanges` in the updates object to `newElementWith`.

After `this.app.scene.replaceAllElements(...)`, if `!isDeleted && updatedTextElement && isTextElement(updatedTextElement) && this.app.state.editingTextElement?.id === updatedTextElement.id && ((_elementHadRanges) || (updatedTextElement.textStyleRanges?.length ?? 0) > 0)`, update `(this.app.state as Mutable<AppState>).editingTextElement = updatedTextElement` so `appState.editingTextElement` stays synchronised without scheduling an extra React render on unstyled text.

2. In `resolveColorTarget`, check `const hasInlineSelection = !!appState.editingTextElement && !!getActiveTextWysiwygSelection(editingText && isTextElement(editingText) ? editingText : appState.editingTextElement);`.

3. When `hasInlineSelection && property === "backgroundColor"`, set `kind = "regular"` so `DEFAULT_ELEMENT_BACKGROUND_PICKS` (with `"transparent"`) is offered and `excludedColors` is `undefined` even when editing a sticky-note label.

value.behaviour: Make `actionChangeStrokeColor` and `actionChangeBackgroundColor` apply and reflect inline `textStyleRanges` when a WYSIWYG substring selection is active, and render inline highlight controls while editing text.
rules: 1. Import `applyTextStyleRange`, `getSelectionTextStyle`, and `isStickyNoteBoundText` from `@excalidraw/element`, and import `getActiveTextWysiwygSelection` from `../wysiwyg/textWysiwyg`.

2. In `actionChangeStrokeColor.perform`, if `appState.editingTextElement` is active, resolve `editingText = elementsMap.get(appState.editingTextElement.id) ?? appState.editingTextElement`; if `isTextElement(editingText)` and `const selection = getActiveTextWysiwygSelection(editingText)` is non-null, compute `nextRanges = applyTextStyleRange(editingText.textStyleRanges, editingText.originalText.length, selection, { strokeColor: color }, editingText.strokeColor)`, update only `editingText` in `elements` with `newElementWith(el, { textStyleRanges: nextRanges }, true)`, and return `{ elements: nextElements, appState: { ...appState, ...appStateUpdates, editingTextElement: nextEditingTextElement }, captureUpdate: CaptureUpdateAction.IMMEDIATELY }` without mutating element-level `strokeColor`, sticky-note ink, or `currentItem*` defaults.

3. In `actionChangeStrokeColor.PanelComponent`, resolve `editingText = appState.editingTextElement ? (app.scene.getElement<ExcalidrawTextElement>(appState.editingTextElement.id) ?? appState.editingTextElement) : null` and `selection = editingText && isTextElement(editingText) ? getActiveTextWysiwygSelection(editingText) : null`; when `selection` is non-null, pass `getSelectionTextStyle(editingText, selection).strokeColor` as `color` to `ColorPicker`; also when `editingText && isTextElement(editingText) && !isStickyNoteBoundText(editingText, app.scene.getNonDeletedElementsMap())`, render `{app.actionManager.renderAction("changeBackgroundColor")}` after `ColorPicker` so inline highlight controls are available while editing any non-sticky text element.

4. In `actionChangeBackgroundColor.perform`, if `appState.editingTextElement` is active, resolve `editingText = elementsMap.get(appState.editingTextElement.id) ?? appState.editingTextElement`; if `isTextElement(editingText)` and `const selection = getActiveTextWysiwygSelection(editingText)` is non-null, compute `nextRanges = applyTextStyleRange(editingText.textStyleRanges, editingText.originalText.length, selection, { backgroundColor: color }, editingText.strokeColor)`, update only `editingText` in `elements` with `newElementWith(el, { textStyleRanges: nextRanges }, true)`, and return `{ elements: nextElements, appState: { ...appState, ...appStateUpdates, editingTextElement: nextEditingTextElement }, captureUpdate: CaptureUpdateAction.IMMEDIATELY }` without mutating container/sticky-note `backgroundColor` or `currentItem*` defaults.

5. In `actionChangeBackgroundColor.PanelComponent`, resolve `editingText = appState.editingTextElement ? (app.scene.getElement<ExcalidrawTextElement>(appState.editingTextElement.id) ?? appState.editingTextElement) : null` and `selection = editingText && isTextElement(editingText) ? getActiveTextWysiwygSelection(editingText) : null`; when `selection` is non-null, pass `getSelectionTextStyle(editingText, selection).backgroundColor` as `color` to `ColorPicker`.
